title: Identity Map

validation.research: Six authoritative source notes. Fowler’s Identity Map catalog entry in Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture establishes identity-key lookup and object reuse within a business operation. Official SQLAlchemy documentation supports identity namespaces, query-result caching distinctions, retention choices, sequential session ownership, and separate expiration/refresh behavior. Python documentation supports the demonstration’s SQLite connection configuration. The article distinguishes identity reuse from persistence, database freshness, isolation, change tracking, and authorization. The contact scenario, code, and native diagrams are original teaching material.
validation.python_examples: Both actual article fences execute as contacts.py and demo.py and produce seven stated lines exactly. Checks cover shared object references, one SELECT per successfully loaded ID, visible local mutation without persistence, positive integer ID and printable-name boundaries, read-only public identity, missing rows without negative caching, a row appearing after an earlier miss, separate objects for distinct IDs with the same name, invalid hydration without registration, repair and successful retry, single-use lifecycle, cleared registries on normal/exceptional exit, strong-reference retention and release, surviving external references, caller-owned connection and transaction, independent database namespaces, closed-connection storage failure, actual external updates/deletion through a second SQLite connection, stale hits, and new instances across scopes. No automatic persistence, refresh, concurrency coordination, or cross-scope object reuse is claimed.

example_limits: Python 3.10+ and standard-library SQLite. One connection and one mapped Contact type make the identity namespace implicit; keys are positive integer IDs, excluding booleans. Names are 1–80 printable nonblank characters. A primary-key miss selects, validates, constructs, and registers; a hit returns the identical object without SQL. Missing rows are not cached. Strong references last until context exit, then the single-use scope clears its map. Outside references can survive. Caller owns connection and transactions; the map issues no save, commit, rollback, or close. Sequential use is required. No query-result API, relationship-cycle hydration, dirty tracking, writes, refresh/expiration, authorization, expected versions, automatic retry, concurrent check/load synchronization, or distributed cache is supplied. New-scope observations still depend on database isolation.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, push, or pull request.
